messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOPAGER fired for infra.gpu-node-47 (gpu-host-47.redwood-prod) - KERNEL_PANIC detected, kubelet NotReady. PagerDuty incident id PD-78912. Auto-fanout to eng-oncall.

pagerduty: PD alert: gpu-host-47 (host: 10.34.5.47) — Unreachable / kernel oops. Escalation policy: oncall-engineering -> oncall-sre.

alice: acked. I'm on it. grabbing serial console and checking logs.

alice: quick check: kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-host-47
```
# output (from control-plane cache)
gpu-host-47   NotReady   1d   v1.27.2   node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu
```

alice: journalctl -k shows a stack trace then "Kernel panic - not syncing" around the same window. posting snippet.
```
[ 4591.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=2345, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 4591.456789] kernel: NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
[ 4591.567890] kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
```

alice: kubelet logs around that time: "Node not ready: KubeletReadiness probe failed; last seen: kernel panic". Pods on that host show Terminating / Unknown.

carmen: do we have customer impact? I see a bump in 5xxs for the hosted-inference-prod route in the last 3m, ~4.8% error rate and latency spike. Router stats show requests were routed to the host for pinned customers (some dedicated-tenants pinned).

dave: nginx/proxy shows upstream timeout for model-serving pods that were on gpu-host-47. A few requests retried successfully on fallback hosts, but some dedicated pinned nodes have no spare capacity -> 503s.

jen: support ticket #INC-4421 just came in: "Our inference calls are failing intermittently, ~10% errors since 10:18 UTC". Customer is on Dedicated cluster with pin to gpu-host-47.

alice: ok immediate plan: cordon gpu-host-47, start evacuation of pods. We'll prefer graceful drain but force when stuck. Also trigger hardware team for RMA / power-cycle if serial indicates hardware fault.

alice: running: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-47 && kubectl drain gpu-host-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60`

alice: drain output: some model-worker pods in Terminating stuck >10s due to kernel panic during checkpoint write, had to `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0` for three pods. Evacuation is progressing; most replicas started on other gpu-hosts.

bob: joining. I'm taking secondary owner for remediation. I'll run IPMI reboot once hardware team confirms cold-reboot allowed. If nvram/GPU bus error persists we may need host replacement.

carmen: rolling capacity increase: proactively bump autoscaler target for dedicated pool serving critical tenants by +2 nodes to absorb pinned load. This will reduce 503s while we wait for replacement.

alice: setting annotations on incident: impact: "partial degraded serving for subset of dedicated tenants; ~5% error rate, some latency increase." tagging PD with severity: SEV2 for customer-visible errors.

incident-bot: Incident PD-78912 created by autopager. Current assignees: alice (ack), bob (escalation). Incident runbook: gpu-host-failure -> cordon/drain -> hw-rma.

bob: hardware team (cc @hw-ops) — requesting IPMI power cycle for host gpu-host-47 (BMC reachable, last sensor temps normal, but PCI shows Xid79). Approving reboot?

hw-ops (via bob): powercycle approved. Scheduling immediate cold reset; ETA 3m.

bob: running `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.34.5.247 -U admin -P **** power cycle` (BMC proxyed). Serial console shows POST then hang at nvme probe... looks like NVMe controller failing during boot. We'll capture dmesg and then RMA.

alice: customer comms: drafting note for support: "We're investigating elevated errors for a subset of dedicated customers pinned to a GPU host; we've drained the host and are routing traffic to spare capacity. We'll follow up with ETA for replacement." Sending now.

carmen: monitoring: adding an eval set to detect regressions after drain. Set alert: if hosted route 5xx >3% for 5m -> page oncall.

dave: proxy routing fallback: enabled strict-fallback-mode for dedicated pool so pinned traffic can failover to a warmed standby for the next 30m. Might increase latency but reduces 503s.

bob: host reboot failed to fully initialize — nvme controller never enumerated. Hardware confirmed suspect NVMe / PCI riser. RMA ticket HW-2218 opened, ETA parts 48-72h.

alice: since replacement will be slow, plan B: reprovision capacity and migrate pinned tenants to a different rack. Ops, can you expedite tenant move?

jen: support updated customer with current status and mitigation (failover enabled). Customer asked for ETA for full recovery; we gave 48-72h worst-case and suggested applying temporary pin to fallback pool managed by us.

bob: handing off active remediation to oncall-night (bob -> alice_night), leaving runbook and commands in the incident doc. I'll continue to monitor until RMA confirmed.

alice: thanks. Summarizing action items: 1) hw-ops RMA HW-2218 (in progress). 2) prod-ops to migrate pinned tenants to fallback pool. 3) eng-infra to watch autoscaler and rollback bump when steady. 4) SRE to monitor error rate and confirm customer regression tests pass.

alice: reassigning incident in PD to alice_night for overnight watch. Ending live handoff here — please DM if urgent. :white_check_mark:
